subject: Retention boundaries for prompt derivatives and model outputs
messages:
From: Sarah Patterson <sarah.patterson@acmeanalytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on what you retain by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Jonas,

Hope you are well. We're working through our internal privacy assessment and need a clear statement for procurement: for Redwood's hosted API, what exactly do you retain by default (full request and response text, prompt tokens, model outputs, and any derived artifacts like embeddings or rerank scores)?

Our legal team wants to know:
- Are raw prompts persisted? If so, for how long?
- Are model-generated outputs stored separately from telemetry?
- Do you consider embeddings/reranks as "derived customer content" and do those persist?

If you have a short written summary we can point procurement/legal to, that would be great. Thanks — Sarah

Regards,
Sarah Patterson
Head of Data Partnerships
Acme Analytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patterson <sarah.patterson@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you retain by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list of questions. Looping in Laura (Legal / Compliance) and Grace (Product) to confirm final language — below is a succinct summary I can share with Procurement once you OK the tone.

Tentative customer-facing summary (draft):
- Default hosted behavior: Redwood stores request metadata and short-term request/response artifacts to support product functionality and abuse detection.
- Prompts/inputs: by default, full request text (prompts) is retained for 30 days and accessible to the customer and our support/ops team when investigating incidents.
- Model outputs: generated outputs are retained for 30 days by default; after that they are purged unless a customer enables longer retention in settings.
- Derived artifacts: embeddings and rerank scores are retained for 30 days by default; they are treated as derived customer content.
- Private/Dedicated: for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can configure retention or opt out of storage entirely.

Laura/Grace — can you confirm whether the 30-day default above is still the official policy and whether we should call out telemetry/aggregated logs separately?

If that works, Sarah — I'll attach a short PDF summary and our SOC2 evidence request template.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you retain by default (prompts vs outputs)

Jonas — quick clarifications for an external-safe summary (this message is internal only):

Authoritative points to use for customer-facing language:
- Hosted API defaults:
  * Request/response content (prompts and outputs): retained for 30 days by default. This includes both the raw prompt text and the model's returned tokens.
  * Derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank scores, similarity indexes): retained for 30 days by default and treated as "derived customer content."
  * Telemetry and operational logs (latency, error traces, token counts): retained in anonymized or aggregated form for 12 months to support SLA and platform analytics. These telemetry logs do not contain full customer prompts by default.
- Opt-out / configuration:
  * Customers on Hosted can request shorter retention or opt-out of storing prompts/outputs — we currently offer a 0/7/30-day selection for hosted tenants; the request goes through Support/SE and has a verification step.
  * Dedicated/Private customers: retention is configurable by the customer; on-prem/VPC installs default to customer-controlled storage and we do not retain customer content on our control plane unless explicitly contracted.
- Deletion and purge paths:
  * Customers can request an immediate purge for their account; our platform runs an account-scoped purge that removes stored request/response artifacts within 48 hours of an approved request (audit trail retained separately).
  * Internal caches (KV cache, inference ephemeral state used to serve streaming responses) are ephemeral and not materialized to long-term storage; they are not part of retention guarantees.
- Security notes for procurement: we can provide SOC 2 artefacts and a short summary PDF (redwood-retention-summary.pdf). For procurement questionnaires, use language above and point them to our SOC2 evidence package.

Jonas — feel free to send the sanitized version to Sarah. I'm attaching the SOC2 evidence template for reference.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOC2_evidence_request_template.pdf]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patterson <sarah.patterson@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you retain by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the question and for giving us a chance to be explicit. Per our internal policy (summarized below), here's what Redwood's hosted API retains by default:

Summary (customer-facing):
- Prompts / request text: retained for 30 days by default. Customers may request shorter retention (0 or 7 days) via Support for hosted tenants.
- Model outputs: retained for 30 days by default, then purged unless longer retention is configured.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank scores): treated as derived customer content and retained for 30 days by default.
- Telemetry / aggregated logs: anonymized telemetry (token counts, latency traces) kept up to 12 months for operational needs; this telemetry does not contain full prompts in its anonymized form.
- Dedicated/Private: retention is customer-configurable; on-premises deployments default to customer-managed storage with no Redwood retention unless contracted.

If you want an official statement to attach to your procurement packet, please use the attached PDF (redwood-retention-summary.pdf). If Procurement needs an account-level purge after contract signing, we can expedite and provide an audit trail within 48 hours after approval.

Next steps? If this looks good I'll loop in our Security team for a short call with your legal/procurement team to answer any follow-ups.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
